speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the onset, duration, and specific characteristics of your double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To help me narrow this down, have you noticed any muscle weakness in your shoulders or arms, and do you experience any swallowing difficulties or slurred speech?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.

The pattern of diplopia worsening with specific gaze (up/down) and significant fatigability of proximal muscles that improves with rest is highly characteristic of Myasthenia Gravis. Have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids (ptosis) or difficulty swallowing?
